summary: A Kubernetes-first chaos platform with strong production safety guardrails: policy-as-code, approvals/audit, progressive rollout with health gates, and an independent kill path enforced by cluster agents with TTL-based fail-safe rollback. It intentionally minimizes moving parts by using Postgres as the durable source of truth and work queue, with agents emitting aggregated run events to control event volume.
strengths: Safety-first execution model (blast radius limits, approvals/audit, monotonic kill generation, agent TTL rollback) with clear failure-mode handling
Operationally pragmatic architecture (few services, durable state machine checkpoints, idempotent steps, event-volume controls) that should be maintainable by a small team
weaknesses: Postgres-centric design (work queue + run state + kill generation + events) risks becoming a bottleneck or shared failure domain at higher event/start rates without careful partitioning and backpressure
Kill path is not fully independent if Postgres or its connectivity is impaired; the document doesn’t fully specify how agents behave when they can’t read kill state and TTLs haven’t yet expired
